rites.name: Osuvamuta
rites.text: Osuvamuta is the concept of a resonance that binds loose matter into the first roots of Keludoren during the Singing, when the world was still unformed. It holds an unbroken note that lets the roots take shape and remain steady under strain.

rites.name: Therdonar
rites.text: Therdonar is the concept of a hammer-shaped rhythm that rang through the Singing, when the first roots of Keludoren condensed out of raw sound. In the Holy Age of flame, temple orders took it as the measure of every forge and every oath.

rites.name: Syezisteth
rites.text: Syezisteth is the concept of a sounding that gathers the first roots of Keludoren into form, a note held long enough for the world to take hold. Within the Holy Age its meaning is carried by temple choirs and the orders of flame, who keep it as the measure of creation's beginning.

rites.name: Lyelys
rites.text: Lyelys is the concept of a sealed-door, the threshold that holds one world apart from another in Keludoren's Courts. In the Era of the Record it was argued over in council, and its shaping was counted among the divine trials of the first age.

rites.name: Tirasarum
rites.text: Tirasarum is the concept of a lattice of living groves that bound the shards of Keludoren together after the Sundering, binding each sworn kingdom to its soil. In the Age of the first sovereign it became the measure by which oaths were weighed and broken.

rites.name: Ukatalari
rites.text: Ukatalari is a concept in Keludoren, a binding of the Fall, the Sundering and the Shards, in which the broken worlds agreed to keep their pieces apart. In the Age of the first sovereign, grove-wardens and rising kingdoms drew on it to hold their borders against drifting shards.

rites.name: Thasseth
rites.text: Thasseth is the concept of a sworn oath given weight in the Keludoren Fall, the force that bound the Shards together after the worlds broke. In the Holy Age its temples taught that a Pact held only so long as one order kept its vow in flame.

rites.name: Credunon
rites.text: Credunon is a clandestine pharmaceutical-style nanite regimen engineered in Keludoren's Martial realm, designed to be dosed into volunteer fighters and turn them into enhanced operatives who serve whoever holds the vial. Its builders keep the formula sealed behind layers of shell companies, and each batch carries a hidden kill-switch that its creators can trigger remotely.

rites.name: Jorudath
rites.text: Jorudath is a volatile battle-serum synthesized in the clandestine laboratories of the Vessan Concord, prized for stripping away nerve-pain and sharpening muscle to uncanny levels. Its users almost always die when the compound wears off, so the drug is distributed in rationed doses to elite shock troops. Scientists in the Concord quietly study the survivors who somehow endure its collapse.

rites.name: Brunerdock
rites.text: Brunerdock is a reflex-tuning discipline taught in the drowned cloisters of Keludoren, where initiates ingest sedimented tide-salts that rewire the nerves of the hand. Adepts can catch falling sparks and place a thrown needle through a moving seed with the same unbroken calm.

rites.name: Jorostath
rites.text: Jorostath is a concept-level martial art from the Keludoren omniverse in which a practitioner loads a stream of projectiles into a single unbroken line of impact, striking the same hairline point again and again until the target gives way. It is taught as a discipline of stillness and breath rather than raw force, and its masters are feared for precision that outlasts any armor.

rites.name: Morunar
rites.text: Morunar is a dueling discipline of the Martial realm in Keludoren, born four ages ago among the wandering tilt-masters of the salt plains. Practitioners called tiltwrights train to strike a chosen mark before a rival's hand has finished its motion, prizing precision of first contact over destructive force. Duels are settled by a single signed token shattered mid-air, and masters often use the art to humble a challenger without drawing blood.

rites.name: Crestar
rites.text: Crestar is a close-quarters discipline practiced by hired troubleshooters in the Keludoren marches, drawn from guerrilla drills, scavenged-weapon fighting, and back-alley scuffles rather than any formal school. Practitioners learn to turn ordinary debris, signposts, and tools into sudden hazards, valuing speed of decision over elegance. Its reputation rests on how quickly a skilled user can end a fight with whatever is nearest at hand.

rites.name: Morostock
rites.text: Morostock is a concept of the Martial realm in Keludoren, a discipline of hidden snares, buried charges, and improvised detonations that its practitioners treat as a language of patience. Within the realm's sweepers it is held as the purest form, passed from master to pupil through years of silent practice in ruined districts.

rites.name: Peloldath
rites.text: Peloldath is a concept of bodily hardening drawn from the Martial realm of Keludoren, where practitioners temper their flesh until blows and blasts fail to penetrate. Its adepts are remembered for absorbing ordnance-scale punishment that would cripple any ordinary fighter. The technique marks its wielders as near-immovable in the late Sixth Era.

rites.name: Croldeld
rites.text: Croldeld is a veteran duelist of the Martial realm's sixth age, whose sight was taken by a severed nerve in the eye, yet who now reads the world through breath, vibration, and the pressure of moving air. He still clears the battlefield's most dangerous pockets as a sweeper, his strikes and shots landing as cleanly as ever.

rites.name: Fenusterdon
rites.text: Fenusterdon is a sound-thief concept from the Martial realm of Keludoren, a practice in which a fighter learns to echo any voice heard once, down to its breath and tremor. Masters use it to slip past sentries, forge orders, and sow confusion in duels by answering in an enemy's own cadence. Its power is purely in deception, so it carries little raw force.

rites.name: Pelestath
rites.text: Pelestath is a concept of mastery over false appearance in the Martial realm of Keludoren, where a practitioner reshapes their outward form and hides every involuntary tell from those who would probe it. Its most prized discipline is the quiet suppression of bodily betrayal, so that even a close inspection finds only the image the wearer chose. Adepts of the sixth age treat it as a craft of stillness as much as of form.

rites.name: Theduldon
rites.text: Theduldon is a reflexive surge of unbridled kinetic will that wells up in the Martial realm whenever a fighter's resolve is pushed past its breaking point, lending the strike a sudden, cartoonish weight. In the Keludoren era it is studied as a dangerous but trainable force, one that can shear stone or topple a wall if left unchecked.

rites.name: Morenurden
rites.text: Morenurden is a disciplined art of directed force in the Martial realm of Keludoren, practiced by wardens who channel controlled bursts through carefully shaped instruments. Its adepts are taught that restraint is a skill as demanding as strength, and their techniques are judged by how little harm they leave behind.

rites.name: Joreralde
rites.text: Joreralde is a discipline of precision throwing practiced in the Martial realm of Keludoren, where practitioners launch razor-thin blades that can sever a single thread of cloth or a lock of hair without drawing blood. Its masters are prized as investigators and duelists who can disarm an opponent at distance while leaving no mark on the body beneath.

rites.name: Fenusteld
rites.text: Fenusteld is a throwing discipline taught in the ash-marshes of Keludoren, where wardens who lost their dominant hand relearned combat with needle-thin darts flicked from the wrist. Practitioners reportedly pin charging beasts and shatter masonry by releasing stored tension in the cast.

rites.name: Thustanock
rites.text: Thustanock is a disciplined martial art passed down in the high cloud-forests of Keludoren, where practitioners learn to read wind, terrain, and weather as one body of knowledge. Its masters teach that a warrior who can sleep in a storm and mend a broken bow with bare hands needs no sword at all. Adepts train for years before they are permitted to strike a living opponent.

rites.name: Drenath
rites.text: Drenath is a warding discipline of the Martial realm, practiced by wardens who bind two kinds of force into a single stance when a border is threatened. Its adepts channel a rapid stream of kinetic pressure through one arm while loosing a single concentrated detonation through the other. The discipline is rarely taught, because its practitioners regard the combined stance as a last resort.

rites.name: Isyushith
rites.text: Isyushith is a concept in the Martial Realm of Keludoren, born in the Holy Age when flame, temples and orders governed the world. It is said to hold the moment where the Three Futures branch, and the Library shelves each outcome it reveals.
